title: Break the Spell of the Tell
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece diagnoses a dysfunctional pattern the author calls the 'TELL' organization, in which leaders, teachers, and parents habitually direct others rather than let them act on their own. Over time, that pattern trains capable people into helplessness, since they learn it is always safer to wait for instructions than to take initiative. The article argues that TELL is efficient in the short term but corrosive over time, because once it becomes the default, other approaches stop working. Breaking the cycle requires leaders to keep setting goals from the top while handing execution to the team, and to tolerate the discomfort of watching people perform imperfectly while they relearn how to act independently. The piece frames this as slow, patient work rather than a quick fix.
points: Constantly telling people what to do creates learned helplessness in both children and adults.
Once a team defaults to being told, other management approaches stop working.
Breaking the pattern means keeping goals top-down but pushing execution decisions to the team.
Expect early execution to be rough as people relearn how to act without direction.
The article frames escaping the TELL pattern as a gradual, deliberate leadership discipline.
quotes: Team leaders push, prod, and cajole people to get them to act. Yet, people wait for instructions.
For leaders, TELL is the faster and most efficient way to get others to do what you want them to.
Leaders who vacillate between directing others and then giving them the freedom to act on their own confuse everyone
Breaking the pattern of TELL requires a tremendous amount of patience on everyone’s part.
Stepping back and watching people execute can be tremendously painful.
Once deprogrammed from the TELL, people regain the ability to act on their own, without waiting for instructions.
